decision: KEEP (trusted-core-confidence design decision 3, Open Question 1 open for the owner). openspec/specs/agent-identity/spec.md requires resource_indicators_supported: true in the discovery document. A rename changes the wire format.

decision: KEEP. Same decision as in the Config OP plan (Open Question 1).
comment: The Dynamic OP plan checks the metadata in this module only.

decision: KEEP. token_type is the token-type guard: the spec oidc-provider makes the ID-token signer refuse any other token_type, and each validator checks it. tid names the realm (spec rbac-token-claims). scope is the granted scope. OIDC Core 2 allows other claims in the ID token, and a removal changes the wire format.
comment: check-export.py fails the run if this warning names any other claim.

decision: KEEP. Hearth puts email and email_verified in the ID token when the email scope is granted, so a relying party does not need a UserInfo call. OIDC Core 5.4 does not forbid it. A removal changes the wire format.
KEEP. Same decision as for oidcc-scope-email.

KEEP. The test user has a display name only, and Hearth has no store for most profile claims (middle_name, nickname, picture, website, gender, birthdate, zoneinfo, locale, updated_at). OIDC Core 5.3.2: a claim with no value is omitted.
KEEP. Hearth does not support the claims request parameter (OIDC Core 5.5 is optional, and discovery does not advertise claims_parameter_supported). The module asks for name with that parameter only.
KEEP. Hearth does not support acr_values and issues no acr claim; the ID token carries amr. OIDC Core 3.1.2.1: acr_values is a voluntary claim request, and the acr claim is a SHOULD.
KEEP. UserInfo takes the access token in the Authorization header only. RFC 6750 2.2 (the token in the form body) is a MAY, and a token in a body is easier to log by mistake.
